correctness.rationale: The final theorem is proved for each fixed c>0, 0<r<1, kappa>0 with ry>c. H_c(z)=z-c-c log(z/c) increases for z>c, uniquely defining y>c and a=1-c/y, b=r-c/y in 0<b<a. For m=floor(c log n), the last-Poisson-term backward geometric sum tends uniformly to (1-c/w)^(-1) at z=w log n+O(log log n), w>c, and Stirling gives log Q_m(z)=-H_c(w) log n-(1-c/w)(z-w log n)-1/2 log log n+O(1). Floor oscillation only affects bounded terms. Inverting n Q_m(u_n)=1 yields u_n=y log n-(log log n)/(2a)+O(1); applying the estimate at ru_n yields log Q_m(ru_n)=-delta log n-eta log log n+O(1) with eta=(1-b/a)/2, proving M_n=Theta(n^delta(log n)^eta), 0<delta<1. Local tail ratios have slopes a,b. Poisson thinning produces independent Gamma(m,1) and Gamma(m,r) clocks, whose bounded-window binomial rare-event laws converge to independent Poisson point processes with intensities a e^(-ax), kappa b e^(-bx). Upper/lower localization bounds permit passing to the maximum and its a.s. unique class; direct integration gives the stated winner probability. Exact event-class identity and conditional variance of the independent Poisson clock at T_n prove (S_{T_n}-T_n)/D_n=o_p(1), since T_n=O_p(D_n log n) and D_n~n. For any alternative L_n, comparing slow and fast clocks at u_n plus/minus fixed thresholds proves each sharp side of the phase transition; the common normalizer does not affect winner. No finite diagnostic is an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality of the complete *marked sharp sparse-class crossover* survives full-text comparisons. The pre-existing public mirror of the exact assigned finding is not independent prior coverage and is excluded from novelty support. General colored Poisson tools are standard, so novelty here is in explicit regime calibration and its marked outcome, not in Poisson thinning. value.rationale: The logarithmically growing repeated-quota collector has a natural competition between n faster coupons and a sublinear population of genuinely slower coupons. The result pinpoints a mathematically motivated sparse threshold with both power exponent delta and nonzero logarithmic correction eta that cannot be removed without changing the limiting class competition. At the boundary two distinct gamma extreme slopes coexist, yielding a non-affine-Gumbel time CDF and a strict 0<P(last slow)<1 mark; below and above, the winner class flips with probability tending to one. These statements quantify an unknown and useful structural scarcity-versus-rate transition, rather than a numerical sample, arbitrary slice, routine renaming or mere reproduction of the marginal scalar transfer theorem. General methods are standard but deriving the explicit critical scale and marked last-class transition is substantive.
residual_risks: Value pertains to new marked sharp-threshold specialization, not to common Poisson thinning or previously-covered unmarked general transfer.
If a stronger existing exact theorem were found to imply this entire threshold/marked law, originality and independent scientific value would require reassessment.

limitations: Fixed c>0, 0<r<1, kappa>0 and ry>c only. Boundary ry=c and ry<c excluded and may require different scales.
Critical population has Theta(n^delta (log n)^eta), not universal convergent prefactor, because the floor(c log n) oscillates; exact quantile M_n resolves this.
No uniform parameter error bound, full heterogeneous-vector classification or expectation expansion is established.
The marginal completion CDF is an application of Long 2026 general unmarked defect theorem; novelty is assessed only for sharp sparse-group scale plus colored mark.
Priority remains best-of-knowledge, not independent historical certification; partial-access quota papers remain explicit residual risks.
Finite computations and existing verification script are corroboration, not the proof of weak convergence.
